topic: How do we know? (valid means of knowledge)
intro: Schools list different pramanas — valid means of knowledge — and this shapes what each can claim to know about the self, God and the world.

rows.claim: Perception alone is valid (as usually reported).
rows.detail: Inference cannot be trusted because we cannot establish that a general rule has no exceptions. Some later materialists may have allowed inference about perceptible matters.
Perception grasps unique momentary particulars; inference works with general concepts. Madhyamaka questions whether pramanas can be established independently.

rows.claim: Two: perception and inference; testimony is treated as inference.
rows.detail: Classical Vaisheshika reduces other means to inference; the later combined school adopted Nyaya's four.

rows.claim: Three: perception, inference and reliable testimony.
rows.detail: Prakriti and purusha, being beyond perception, are established by inference; testimony covers the rest.
Yoga accepts Sankhya's three pramanas, listing valid knowledge as one of the fluctuations of mind to be stilled.

rows.claim: Direct and indirect knowledge, qualified by many-sided standpoints.
rows.detail: Knowledge is classified into five kinds, from sensory to omniscient. Anekantavada holds any claim is true only from a particular standpoint.

rows.claim: Four: perception, inference, comparison and testimony.
rows.detail: Nyaya gives a detailed theory of each, a five-membered inference, and holds that validity is confirmed by external checks.

rows.claim: Up to six; knowledge is intrinsically valid unless defeated.
rows.detail: Kumarila accepts six, adding postulation and non-apprehension; Prabhakara accepts five. Only the Veda reveals dharma.

rows.claim: Six pramanas; scripture alone reveals Brahman.
rows.detail: Advaita largely follows Kumarila for the everyday world, but holds that Brahman, not being an object, is known only through the Upanishadic teaching.

note: The debate is less about counting sources than about their limits: whether anything beyond perception can be known, whether reason can reach God or the Self, and whether scripture is a distinct and authoritative source.
